Let

\[
S=\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\sum_{j=1}^{100}2^{-\left\lfloor 101k/j\right\rfloor}.
\]

Set \(p=101\) and \(x=2^{-1}\). For a fixed \(j\), write \(k=r+jt\) with \(1\le r\le j\) and \(t\ge0\). Then

\[
\left\lfloor \frac{p(r+jt)}{j}\right\rfloor
=
\left\lfloor \frac{pr}{j}\right\rfloor+pt.
\]

Hence

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}x^{\lfloor pk/j\rfloor}
=
\frac{1}{1-x^p}\sum_{r=1}^j x^{\lfloor pr/j\rfloor}.
\]

So

\[
S=\frac{1}{1-x^{101}}F,
\]

where

\[
F=\sum_{j=1}^{100}\sum_{r=1}^j x^{\lfloor 101r/j\rfloor}.
\]

Now write

\[
F=\sum_{m=1}^{101}c_m x^m.
\]

Because \(101\) is prime, the coefficients are:

\[
c_m=50 \quad (1\le m\le 99),\qquad c_{100}=0,\qquad c_{101}=100.
\]

Indeed, for \(1\le m\le 99\), the pairs \((j,r)\) with \(\lfloor 101r/j\rfloor=m\) come in complementary pairs \(j\mapsto 101-j\), giving exactly \((101-1)/2=50\) for each \(m\). The value \(m=101\) occurs when \(r=j\), giving \(100\) pairs, and \(m=100\) occurs never.

Thus

\[
F=50\sum_{m=1}^{99}2^{-m}+100\cdot 2^{-101}.
\]

Since

\[
\sum_{m=1}^{99}2^{-m}=1-2^{-99},
\]

we get

\[
F=50(1-2^{-99})+100\cdot 2^{-101}
=50-\frac{25}{2^{99}}
=\frac{25(2^{100}-1)}{2^{99}}.
\]

Therefore

\[
S
=
\frac{F}{1-2^{-101}}
=
\frac{25(2^{100}-1)}{2^{99}}
\cdot
\frac{2^{101}}{2^{101}-1}
=
\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{100(2^{100}-1)}{2^{101}-1}}
\]
